## Participation and data collection

We collected weight data in two Open Data Kit forms: an enrolment form carrying all characteristics, and a follow-up form carrying date and weight only, both identified by the participant's anonymised ID.

### Exclusion criteria

Exclusions were dominated by 214 (20%) follow-up records that we could not link to a previously enrolled participant (see below).
We also excluded 148 records as duplicates, 37 that refused consent, and 6 for a missing or implausible value (Figure 1A of the manuscript).

#### Unlinked follow-up measurements

We collected 570 follow-up records.
Among valid records, 214 (from 202 participant IDs) did not match any enrolment record participant ID, so we could not identify these with pre-war weight, height or demographics.
Almost all of these unlinked measurements came after the second round of recruitment (86% appeared over 8-12 November 2025; Figure 1B of the manuscript).

These may be participants who entered a different ID combination from their enrolment ID, or who only ever used the follow-up form without enrolling.
Linkage failure was likely partly due to mistyped composite IDs: 68% of follow-up records with a composite ID were unmatched, against 14% of those with a national ID.
All identifiers were stored only as one-way hashes, so mistyped IDs could not be corrected.
At least some of these records also come from people who only ever used the follow-up form.
In the 8-12 November week we saw more unmatched composite IDs (157) than there were participants ever enrolled with a composite ID (137).
Unlinked measurements were also heavier than linked follow-up measurements (median 71 against 66 kg).

### Recruitment and checks for selection bias

Participants enrolled in two cohorts, August-September and October-November 2025 (Figure 1B of the manuscript).

We compared enrolment characteristics by cohort and by whether participants returned for follow-up.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-balance-cohort
#| tbl-cap: "Enrolment characteristics by enrolment cohort."

tbl_balance_cohort |>
  as_ft()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-balance-followup
#| tbl-cap: "Enrolment characteristics by whether the participant contributed any follow-up measurement."

tbl_balance_followup |>
  as_ft()
```

We modelled the odds of contributing any follow-up measurement by participant characteristic (age, sex, residence, dependent children, role, BMI at enrolment and enrolment cohort) with logistic regression.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-return
#| tbl-cap: "Odds of contributing at least one follow-up measurement, by participant characteristic at enrolment."

fit_return |>
  tbl_regression(exponentiate = TRUE, label = labels_for(return_vars)) |>
  modify_column_hide("p.value") |>
  as_ft()
```

Change since pre-war was similar among participants who did or did not contribute follow-up measurements (mean loss 16.5% and 15.3% respectively).
Participants with dependent children had higher odds of returning than those with none (odds ratio 2.20 (1.09-4.42) for one child, similar for two or more), and residents of Gaza City and North Gaza lower odds than residents of Deir Al Balah (0.45 (0.22-0.87)).
Participants in the October-November cohort had much lower odds of returning (0.18 (0.10-0.33)).

```{r}
#| label: fig-bmi-pyramid

bmi_pyramid_plot <- bmi_category_long |>
  filter(!is.na(sex), !is.na(age)) |>
  count(period, sex, age, bmi_category) |>
  mutate(n_signed = if_else(sex == "Male", -n, n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n_signed, y = age, fill = bmi_category)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#01454f", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = abs) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(direction = -1, name = "BMI category", drop = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~period) +
  labs(x = "Participants  (Male <- | -> Female)", y = NULL)

```

### Risk factors for weight change since pre-war

Chronic condition was recorded for only 144 participants, almost all enrolling from late October, so we did not include it in the main adjusted model and analysed it separately among the participants asked.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-chronic
#| tbl-cap: "Difference in weight change since pre-war for participants reporting a chronic condition, adjusted, among those who were asked."

tbl_chronic |>
  as_ft()
```

### Weight change during follow-up

```{r}
#| label: tbl-followup-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Sensitivity of the fitted change in weight over follow-up to model specification and participant selection.
#|   Change: fitted weight on the last day of follow-up minus the first day, percentage points of pre-war weight (delta-method 95% CI).
#|   Main model: smooth of calendar day, linear term for day of enrolment, participant random intercept.
#|   Each other row changes one element, except the last; with participant as a fixed effect, change is averaged over participants.
#|   Adjusted rows: participants with missing sex, age or residence are dropped.
#|   All participants: includes those measured only once, who inform the change only by comparison between participants enrolled at different times.
#|   EDF: effective degrees of freedom of the calendar-day smooth (1 = linear).

followup_sensitivity |>
  transmute(
    Model = model,
    Participants = participants,
    Measurements = measurements,
    Days = days,
    `Change (95% CI)` = change,
    EDF = sprintf("%.2f", edf)
  ) |>
  ft()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-followup-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Diagnostics for the main follow-up model (mgcv::gam.check), on the log scale of weight relative to pre-war.
#|   Top left: quantile-quantile plot of deviance residuals.
#|   Top right: residuals against the linear predictor.
#|   Bottom left: histogram of residuals.
#|   Bottom right: observed against fitted values.
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| results: hide

gam.check(fit_gam)
```

## Population comparisons

### Pre-war BMI

#### 2020 population survey

We compared the pre-war BMI of participants aged 40-59 (the age bands with 10 or more participants) with an independent 2020 survey of a representative sample of the Gaza Strip population in this age group [@abuhamadHypertensionCascadeCare2022].
Participants shared a similar weight distribution; however, mean BMI was lower among women in our sample compared to the representative survey (by 2.1-2.5 kg/m^2^), and higher among men (by 1.5-2.1 kg/m^2^; Table S8).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-external
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Pre-war BMI in this study compared with a 2020 cross-sectional survey of adults aged 40 and over, by age band and sex.
#|   Men aged 60-69 (n = 2) are shown but not included in the comparison in the text.

external_comparison |>
  transmute(
    `Age band` = recode(
      age_band,
      "[40,50)" = "40-49", "[50,60)" = "50-59", "[60,70)" = "60-69", "[70,120]" = "70+"
    ),
    Sex = sex,
    `This study, n` = n_this_study,
    `This study, mean BMI (SD)` = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f)", mean_bmi_prewar, sd_bmi_prewar
    ),
    `2020 survey, mean BMI` = sprintf("%.1f", bmi_2020)
  ) |>
  ft()
```

#### NCD-RisC estimates

We compared the prevalence of underweight and obesity from recalled pre-war weight with modelled prevalence for 2022 [@ncdriscObesityRisePlateaus2026].
For Palestine we used estimates by sex and 5-year age group, weighted to participants' ages; for the world, age-standardised estimates by sex.
We used point estimates only.
Estimates for Palestine include the West Bank.

Among women, we observed similar prevalence of underweight (1.3% in our sample, against 1.4% in the modelled estimate), and lower prevalence of obese BMI (38% and 45% respectively).
Among men, our sample had lower prevalence of underweight (0%, against 2%), but higher prevalence of obese BMI (37%, against 29%), compared to the modelled estimate.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-prewar-reference
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Underweight (BMI < 18.5 kg/m2) and obesity (BMI of 30 kg/m2 or more) from recalled pre-war weight, compared with NCD-RisC modelled prevalence for 2022.
#|   Palestine: by sex and 5-year age group, weighted to participants' ages; includes the West Bank.
#|   World: by sex, age-standardised.
#|   Both sexes are weighted to participants' sex mix.

prewar_reference |>
  mutate(sex = factor(sex, levels = c(sex_levels, "Both"))) |>
  arrange(sex) |>
  transmute(
    Sex = sex,
    n,
    `Underweight, %: recalled` = sprintf("%.1f", underweight_recalled),
    `Underweight, %: Palestine` = sprintf("%.1f", underweight_palestine),
    `Underweight, %: world` = sprintf("%.1f", underweight_world),
    `Obese, %: recalled` = sprintf("%.1f", obese_recalled),
    `Obese, %: Palestine` = sprintf("%.1f", obese_palestine),
    `Obese, %: world` = sprintf("%.1f", obese_world)
  ) |>
  ft()
```

### Adult weight change

#### Comparable estimates of change

We compared weight change in this study with other studies of adults in the Gaza Strip since October 2023 that reported weight before and during the war [@alnabihFoodInsecurityWeight2024; @farisCatastrophicFamineGaza2025].

```{r}
#| label: tbl-literature
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Studies of weight change among adults in the Gaza Strip since October 2023.
#|   Weights and BMI are sample means.
#|   Loss is the difference between mean pre-war and mean current weight, as a percentage of mean pre-war weight, for comparability with the published studies; the mean of individual percentage changes in this study is reported in the manuscript.
#|   Alnabih et al.: no height recorded, so no BMI.

literature_comparison |>
  ft()
```

## Study materials

### Survey questionnaires

We collected data with two Open Data Kit forms, each available in English and Arabic.
Participants first read the information sheet (dated 31 July 2025) and gave consent on the enrolment form; refusing consent ended the form.

Consent statements (yes/no):

- I have read the information sheet dated 31st July 2025 for this project and I have or can access a copy of it if needed.
- I understand that my consent is voluntary and that I am free to withdraw this consent at any time without giving any reason and without my job or legal rights being affected.
- I understand that results from the project may be published in scientific journals or reports, without the use of any information that could identify me.
- I agree to take part in this project by providing data on myself.

Enrolment form:

- Participant ID: either 
  - the 9-digit Palestinian national ID
  - a composite of the initials of first name, family name, father's name and mother's name, date of birth (dd/mm/yy) and the initial of a favourite Palestinian artist (e.g. FASY031178S). 
  - The ID was hashed on the device before upload.
- Organisation
- Date (today by default, with the option to select a past date)
- Date of birth
- Sex (male, female, other/prefer not to say)
- Governorate of current residence (North Gaza, Gaza City, Deir al Balah, Khan Younis, Rafah)
- Role (expatriate staff, national staff, consultant/contractor, casual/daily worker, other, prefer not to say)
- Number of children aged under 10 years in Gaza that the participant is currently responsible for feeding daily
- Estimated height (cm)
- Estimated weight before the war (kg, to 0.1)
- Weight today (kg, to 0.1)
- Chronic health conditions, with free text for "other" (added 10 August 2025)
- Comments (optional free text)

Follow-up form:

- Participant ID, as above
- Date of measurement (today by default, with the option to select a past date)
- Weight on that date (kg, to 0.1)

## Reporting checklist

We report this study following the STROBE guideline for cohort studies [@vonelmStrengtheningReportingObservational2007].

| Item | No. | Recommendation | Where reported |
|------------|----|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Title and abstract | 1a | Indicate the design with a commonly used term | Abstract, Methods ("cohort study") |
| | 1b | Informative and balanced summary | Abstract |
| Background, rationale | 2 | Scientific background and rationale | Introduction |
| Objectives | 3 | Objectives, including prespecified hypotheses | Introduction (three aims); no prespecified hypotheses |
| Study design | 4 | Key elements of design early in the paper | Methods, Study design |
| Setting | 5 | Setting, locations, dates of recruitment, exposure, follow-up and data collection | Methods, Study design (agencies, advertisements in July and October 2025, scales, data entry); Results, Participation (30 July to 1 December 2025) |
| Participants | 6a | Eligibility, sources and methods of selection; methods of follow-up | Methods, Study design (staff and contractors of SCI and UNRWA's Health Section; self-selected after advertisement; voluntary return to measure) |
| | 6b | Matched studies: matching criteria | Not applicable |
| Variables | 7 | Define outcomes, exposures, predictors, confounders, effect modifiers | Methods, Study design (baseline characteristics) and Analysis (outcomes, adjustment set) |
| Data sources, measurement | 8 | Sources of data and methods of assessment | Methods, Study design (calibrated scales, recalled pre-war weight, self-reported height, Open Data Kit forms) |
| Bias | 9 | Efforts to address potential sources of bias | Methods, Analysis (plausibility checks, balance, return for follow-up); Results, Sensitivity analysis; Discussion (recall and selection bias) |
| Study size | 10 | How the study size was arrived at | Not reported: open voluntary recruitment, no sample size calculation |
| Quantitative variables | 11 | Handling of quantitative variables; groupings and why | Methods, Analysis (BMI categories, enrolment cohorts, log weight ratio, combined governorates); Table 1 (age groups) |
| Statistical methods | 12a | All statistical methods, including control for confounding | Methods, Analysis |
| | 12b | Subgroups and interactions | No interaction terms; change by enrolment cohort in Table S4 |
| | 12c | Missing data | Missing counts in Table 1; complete-case analysis, not stated in the text |
| | 12d | Loss to follow-up | Methods, Analysis (logistic regression of return); follow-up model uses all available measurements |
| | 12e | Sensitivity analyses | Methods, Analysis (six refits; Table S7) |
| Participants | 13a | Numbers at each stage of study | Results, Participation; Figure 1A |
| | 13b | Reasons for non-participation at each stage | Figure 1A (exclusions by reason); number of staff invited unknown |
| | 13c | Flow diagram | Figure 1A |
| Descriptive data | 14a | Characteristics of participants; exposures and confounders | Table 1; Tables S1-S2 |
| | 14b | Number with missing data for each variable | Table 1 |
| | 14c | Follow-up time | Results, Weight change over the study period (124-day study period); Table S7 (days and measurements per analysis set) |
| Outcome data | 15 | Numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time | Results, Weight change over the conflict and Weight change over the study period; Figure 2; Tables S4-S5 |
| Main results | 16a | Unadjusted and adjusted estimates with precision; confounders adjusted for | Table 1; Figure 3; Results; Methods, Analysis (adjustment set) |
| | 16b | Category boundaries for categorised continuous variables | Methods, Analysis (BMI categories); Table 1 (age groups) |
| | 16c | Relative risk translated into absolute risk | Results, Weight change over the conflict (underweight 0.7% to 8.1%, relative risk 11.7) |
| Other analyses | 17 | Subgroups, interactions, sensitivity analyses | Tables S3, S6-S10; Figure S2 |
| Key results | 18 | Key results with reference to objectives | Discussion, first paragraph |
| Limitations | 19 | Sources of bias or imprecision; direction and magnitude | Discussion (representativeness, recall and selection bias, participant mix, linkage) |
| Interpretation | 20 | Cautious overall interpretation | Discussion |
| Generalisability | 21 | External validity | Discussion (employment, sex differences) |
| Funding | 22 | Source of funding and role of funders | Funding |
